title: introduce-presubmit-lint-profiling-and-dep-refresh-scheduler
author: Maya Hernandez
release_notes: Adds presubmit lint runtime profiling (no behavior change) and a low-risk dependency refresh scheduler that opens validated candidate PRs during off-peak windows.
description:
Motivation: Presubmit feedback time is the dominant developer productivity drag for many teams. Our lint pipeline runs many rules but we lack visibility into the per-rule cost and which rules are the primary contributors to presubmit latency. At the same time, dependency churn (minor/patch updates) is piling up and manual refreshes create churn and surprise failures. This PR introduces two complementary pieces: (1) lightweight runtime profiling for the presubmit lint runner to surface per-rule latency and hot paths, and (2) a dependency-refresh scheduler that runs candidate bumps in a controlled off-peak window, validates them across the staged test matrix, and opens curated PRs for maintainers.

Design summary: The lint profiler is implemented as a non-blocking instrumentation layer in the presubmit runner. It records rule execution durations, aggregate counts, and slow-rule traces to a compact telemetry blob that is uploaded as a build artifact for failed/passing presubmits. No lint behavior or rule ordering is changed. The dep-refresh scheduler is implemented as a cron-triggered GitHub Action that runs ephemeral containerized upgrades (npm/pip/go modules), applies the minimal lockfile changes, runs a fast smoke pipeline, and if green, opens a draft PR with test traces and a short summary. The scheduler respects repo-configured blackout windows and per-repo exclusion lists.

Implementation notes: - New files: tools/presubmit/profiler.go implements sampling and per-rule timers (uses existing telemetry client). - Action workflow: .github/workflows/dep-refresh-scheduler.yml runs daily at 04:00 UTC and supports a manual dispatch. - New docs: docs/ci/presubmit-profiling.md explains how to interpret profiler artifacts and dashboards. - Config: ci/dep-refresh.yaml allows per-repo rate limits and excluded packages.

Testing and validation: - Unit tests for profiler aggregation logic (pkg/lint/profiler_test.go). - Integration: staged run on a replica repo (redwood-infra/test-repo) with seeded slow rules to validate artifact contents. - CI: initial push failed due to a lint rule (unused-variable) being picked up by a stricter formatter; fixed in second commit. Final CI run: all checks passed (lint, unit, integration smoke matrix). The dep-refresh Action was run in dry-run mode on the test-repo; produced draft PRs and artifacts for inspection.

Rollout plan: Feature flags are used so the profiler can be toggled per-org (default off for enterprise customers); we will enable it opt-in for the redwood org for 2 weeks to collect baseline data. The dep-refresh scheduler starts in dry-run mode for one week and will only create draft PRs; after maintainers signoff we switch to draft+label mode for low-risk automatic PRs. Observability: new dashboard panels and alerting for unusually slow lint rules and for scheduler failure rates (SLO target: 99% successful runs in dry-run mode).

Backward compatibility and safety: No presubmit gating changes are made in this PR. The profiler is read-only for rule results. The dep-refresh scheduler will not merge any changes automatically; PRs are opened in draft state and require human review. Blackout windows and per-repo excludes are enforced to avoid noisy windows or repos with special-release processes.

Follow-ups: - ENG-2016: UI panel to visualize slow-rule trends and suggested rule quarantines. - ENG-2020: automatic suggestion engine that proposes rule splitting/parallelization for the top-3 slow rules. - ENG-2021: integration with the release automation to optionally land low-risk patch bumps on behalf of maintainers.

review_comments: Arjun Patel: Could we sample only 10% of presubmits to start? Profiling every run may add noise. - Response: profiler uses adaptive sampling; default 1% with a toggle in org config. I added sampling config and clarified in docs. (Maya)

Lina Gomez: The action needs a configurable time budget and better cleanup of ephemeral branches. - Response: added timeouts and explicit branch cleanup; action now deletes ephemeral refs on failure. (Maya)

Samir Rao: Can the scheduler respect 'release/*' protected branches? - Response: scheduler now reads repo protection list and skips any repo that has protected branch patterns configured. Added tests. (Maya)
Arjun Patel: Approve after minor test naming nit. (LGTM)
notes_for_release: Introduces observability-only presubmit lint profiling and a non-merging dependency refresh scheduler (dry-run by default). No immediate behavior changes expected. See docs/ci/presubmit-profiling.md for instructions.
post_merge_tasks: graduate dep-refresh from dry-run to draft+label mode
